## Wave 2 Summary

Wave 2 computes the fermion-mass texture cluster that all five S99 review syntheses (lizzi, mack, phonon-first, quantum-foam, volovik) converged on. The S99 fermion-mass panel reframed the generation hierarchy as living in the ε_LX left-invariance-breaking finite-part deformation on the multiplicity bundle — but the literal Dirac-mass overlap integral that Baptista Paper 14 §3 leaves unwritten (the Laplacian matrices are written; the overlap is not) was never computed. The S97 predecessor (`S97-YUKAWA-FAMILY-DERIVE`) returned the multiplicity-scalar result `R_cross_yukawa_t1_t2 = 1.019704` ≈ 1, i.e. a generation-BLIND 1:1:1 envelope against the PDG 1:0.0595:0.000288 — because it used the WRONG observable (lightest-|λ| per sector, not the Higgs-mode overlap). This wave supplies the correct observable: `O_g = ∫_K Tr[ψ_g† |s(h)|² ψ_g] vol_{g_τ}`, the |s(h)|²-weighted Casimir-ladder overlap, computed two independent ways (direct overlap integral; Connes geodesic distance), plus the lepton-only Z₃ phase lever and the Casimir-widening discriminator.

The wave produces FOUR gate verdicts in a fixed within-wave order: **5 → 6 → {7, 8}**. Item 5 (`S100a-DUAL-Z3-PHI-POINTS`, closed-form, runs first, 1–2 h) supplies the dual-Z₃ structure that Item 6 consumes. Item 6 (`S100a-YUKAWA-OVERLAP-OFFDIAG`, the consensus lead) builds the overlap machinery and emits BOTH the diagonal envelope {d_i} and the off-diagonal `w = |w|·e^{i·arg(w)}` in one object. Items 7 (`S100a-CASIMIR-WIDENING`) and 8 (`S100a-CONNES-DISTANCE-LADDER`) run after Item 6's machinery and provide, respectively, the Casimir-ladder widening discriminator and an independent regulator-invariant route to the SAME envelope. Item 6's |w| SOFT-feeds Wave 3 (Item 9 freeze-in fit); Item 6's ε_LX operator SOFT-feeds Wave 4 (Item 14 foam-survival).

**Functional-sensitivity pin (lizzi layer-verdict, carried by the context file)**: the extracted RATIOS (widening, μ:τ:e envelope, off-diagonal phase) are FUNCTIONAL-INDEPENDENT — each gate pre-registers ONE scheme; NO cross-scheme re-runs are prescribed. Only an a₄-pulled |s(h)|² OVERALL SCALE would be functional-dependent (no gate in this wave consumes one; the scale is Wave 4's Item 12 problem, not Wave 2's). The widening, envelope shape, and arg(w) are scheme-invariant ratios by construction.

## Wave 2 → Wave 3 Decision Point

Wave 3 (Items 9–11, the freeze-in / envelope-overdetermination cluster) SOFT-depends on Wave 2's Item-6 `|w|` (the off-diagonal magnitude is a cross-check seed for the `[[d,w],[w*,d]]` block fit; the fit is PDG-self-contained, so the dependency is SOFT, not blocking).

| Wave 2 verdict pattern | Wave 3 consequence |
|:--|:--|
| Item 6 PASS (envelope resolves, widening ∈ band, |w| > 0) | Wave 3 Item 9 freeze-in fit uses the substrate-derived |w| as a cross-check seed against its PDG-fitted |w|; a match strengthens the "one operator, several faces" identification. Items 7 + 8 PASS reinforce the Casimir-ladder envelope shape feeding Item 10's two-way envelope coincidence. |
| Item 6 INFO (envelope direction right, widening needs closure) | Item 7's widening verdict adjudicates the shape; Wave 3 proceeds with the PDG-self-contained fit and treats |w| as fit-output-only (no substrate seed). |
| Item 6 FAIL (1:1:1 recurs) | The ε_LX-on-multiplicity reframe is broken at the diagonal; Wave 3 Item 9's over-constrained freeze-in fit becomes the decisive corridor test — a clean FAIL there closes the dynamical-freeze-in route. The §IV layer-separation ledger (Wave 4) records the corridor closure. |
| Item 7 INFO (W ≈ 1.333) | Sector-assignment correction flagged: Wave 3/4 consumers re-key the tower to the fundamental (k,0) sectors before consuming the widening. |
| Item 8 PASS independent of Item 6 outcome | The Connes route stands as a regulator-invariant envelope anchor regardless of Item 6; if Item 6 FAILed but Item 8 PASSes, the tension itself routes to `/rclab-investigate` as a workshop seed (overlap-route vs Connes-route divergence). |

Within-wave: Items 7 and 8 run AFTER Item 6 lands its `.npz` (Item 7 HARD-depends on the overlap module; Item 8 only soft-cross-checks against it). Item 5 runs FIRST and feeds Item 6's sector-assignment cross-check.
